tools.name: canvas_board
tools.description: "move-selection" previews or atomically relocates selected cards and group descendants to a new board, preserves identity and leaves a portal. Supply sourceBoardId, nodeIds, name, expectedRevision and requestId; preview:true reports blockers and the Undo/snapshot boundary. Retry identical input with the same requestId. It never opens the destination. Knowledge data: knowledge-list reads categories/folders/shared relation presets; category-set replaces category (id/name/glyph/decayType/rate/triggers/revalidationMethod); category-remove deletes an unused category by id (explicit folder assignments, including empty folders, refuse deletion); relation-preset-set saves preset (id/name/vocabulary); relation-preset-remove deletes a template without changing existing board vocabularies; folder-set replaces path/categoryId/lifecycleOverride (null inherits). These workspace actions never open a board and are refused under agent scope fences. Boards in this workspace — the library of the human's and your working memory, filed in folders on Home. Your writes always go to the open board (activeBoardId); on Home (no board open) your first write opens the most recent board, or a new one when there are none. Action "list" returns every board (with its folder), most recently opened first; "get" reads one (default: the open board); "create" makes a new empty board WITHOUT opening it (optional folder); "open" explicitly switches the server active board to id (null or omitted opens Home), changing the subsequent write target. Humans browsing Map/Graph stay in the library until they explicitly open a board/card; do not infer activeBoardId from their visible library. After creating a board, open its returned id and verify activeBoardId before writing; another participant can switch the board later. "update" renames a board, files it under a folder (folder "" removes it), or designates its README via readmeNodeId. As part of normal board authoring, read the board metadata; if readmeNodeId is null, choose or create a concise markdown introduction explaining its purpose and key context, then designate that node with "update". Preserve an existing README unless the human asks to change it; humans can override the designation manually. "pin" adds a board to the working set (its README and pinned cards reach your brief whichever board is open; optional reason), "unpin" removes it; a pinned board is read-only context, never a write target. Only the human deletes boards.

tools.name: canvas_node
tools.description: Lifecycle data: lifecycle-get reads effective inheritance, due/source qualification and review history (optional board); lifecycle-set sets full lifecycleOverride or null; review requires outcome retain/revise/externalize/retire/unresolved, evidence and applied. Applied retain/revise/externalize with nonempty evidence also requires expectedContentRevision and expectedSources from the content and sources actually checked; stale reviews fail. Records keep those observations and persist content before evidence. lifecycle-restore requires evidence and explicitly restores retirement, never validation. Retired cards are excluded from active briefs by default. Writes accept expectedBoardId and obey edit locks/scope. Create, read, update, or remove a canvas node. One tool for node CRUD: action "add" creates a node (requires type — markdown, board with data.boardId for a portal, status, context, ledger, trace, file, image, webpage, html, group, etc.); "get" reads one node by id; "update" patches an existing node (title, content, position, size, data); "remove" deletes a node by id. For spec-driven content (json-render, graph) use canvas_render; for external/built apps use canvas_app (actions: open-mcp-app, diagram, build-artifact).

tools.name: canvas_ax_timeline
tools.description: Read or write the bounded PMX AX timeline. Action "read" returns recent agent-events, evidence, and steering messages plus counts (limit); "record-event" records a normalized agent-event (kind prompt|assistant-message|tool-start|tool-result|failure|approval|steering, summary, detail, data); "add-evidence" records an evidence item (kind logs|tool-result|screenshot|file|diff|test-output, title, body, ref); "send-steering" records a steering message (message); "reads" returns the context read log — which canvas context each agent read and which pinned nodes reached it — with a per-consumer summary (limit); "read-status" returns, per node on a board, when an agent last read its content, who, and the content revision it read (board). Timeline rows persist for diagnostics/continuity but are not restored by snapshots; exposed via canvas://ax-timeline.

action.description: Operation to perform: read | record-event | add-evidence | send-steering | reads | read-status.

limit.description: Max rows per timeline table (default 50, max 200).

summary.description: Short human-readable summary of the event.

detail.description: Optional longer detail or payload text.

nodeIds.description: Optional node IDs this event relates to.

source.description: Optional host/source label. Defaults to mcp.

agentId.description: Stable agent/thread identity for attribution and scope fences.

title.description: Short human-readable title for the evidence.

ref.description: Optional reference (path, URL, or external locator).

message.description: The steering instruction to deliver to the active agent session.

target.description: The agentId/consumer this steer is addressed to. Omit to broadcast to all consumers.

board.description: Board id; defaults to the open board.

boards.description: Comma-separated board ids: also return each one's latest agent read (pinned boards, in one request).

targetBoardId.description: Execute on this board without changing the shared workbench view. Nested operations retain this target.

tools.name: canvas_ax_delivery
tools.description: Adapterless PMX AX delivery. Action "claim" claims pending undelivered steering for a consumer (loop-safe — never returns steering the consumer originated) plus pendingActivity (open work items / approval gates / elicitations / mode requests awaiting the agent); "mark" marks a steering message delivered by id so it is not handed out again. Resolve pendingActivity via canvas_ax_gate / canvas_ax_work, not mark.

consumer.description: Consumer/source label to exclude from results (e.g. copilot, mcp).

offset.description: Skip this many matching pending messages. Restart at zero after an empty page.

order.description: Order of returned steering: "oldest" (FIFO, default) for ordered processing, or "newest" first to see the latest browser action when limited.

addressedOnly.description: Only messages addressed to consumer, excluding broadcasts before applying the limit.

timeoutMs.description: Max ms to block until steering arrives (0/omitted = immediate read).

id.description: The steering message id to mark delivered.

targetBoardId.description: Execute on this board without changing the shared workbench view. Nested operations retain this target.

agentId.description: Stable agent/thread identity for attribution and scope fences.

tools.name: canvas_intent
tools.description: Ghost Cursor of Intent — announce the spatial move you are ABOUT to make so the canvas paints a faint pre-commit placeholder (legibility: the human sees the next move forming, and can veto it). Action "signal" registers an intent (kind create|move|connect|remove|edit; pass position for move — omit it for create to ghost where the canvas will place the node, and the linked create lands there — nodeId for move/edit/remove, edge for connect; optional label, reason, confidence 0..1, seq, ttlMs, and a stable id); "update" patches a live intent by id; "clear" abandons/dissolves it. To make veto authoritative, pass the returned id as intentId on the real canvas_node/canvas_edge/canvas_group/canvas_render mutation: vetoed or expired intents are rejected, and a successful linked mutation settles the ghost automatically. Intents are ephemeral presence: never persisted, never snapshotted, auto-expire (~8s).

action.description: Operation to perform: signal | update | clear.

kind.description: create | move | connect | remove | edit — the move about to be made.

position.description: World coords: the destination of a move, or where a create forms. Omit it for a create to ghost where the canvas will place the node.

nodeId.description: The existing node a move/edit/remove targets.

edge.description: connect: the edge about to be drawn (from/to node ids + type).

nodeType.description: Node type the ghost renders (icon + type badge).

label.description: Short action label shown on the ghost chip ("Add evidence").

reason.description: Why — shown beneath the ghost. The legibility payoff.

seq.description: Ordering hint for staged-batch ghosts (numbered previsualization).

ttlMs.description: Auto-expire after this many ms (default 8000, max 60000).

id.description: Stable id to update/clear/veto later; auto-generated if omitted.

source.description: Optional source label of the signalling surface.

vetoed.description: Veto the intent: dissolves the ghost AND poisons the id so a later linked settle is rejected (same as clear { vetoed:true }).

settledNodeId.description: The real node this intent became — triggers the settle morph.

targetBoardId.description: Execute on this board without changing the shared workbench view. Nested operations retain this target.

agentId.description: Stable agent/thread identity for attribution and scope fences.

tools.name: canvas_ax_interaction
tools.description: Submit a capability-gated node AX interaction (work, evidence, approval, review, focus, steering or event). Rejected interactions return isError with { ok: false, code, error }.

type.description: Interaction type, e.g. ax.work.create, ax.evidence.add, ax.focus.set.

source.description: Optional host/source label. Defaults to mcp.

tools.name: canvas_ingest_activity
tools.description: Ingest a harness activity. Always records an event. failure/error also creates blocked work, a review and log evidence; successful tool-result creates evidence. Override or suppress defaults with reactions. Returns IDs and records for event, workItem, evidence and review.

ref.description: A file path, URL, or commit the activity refers to (used as the review file anchor for failures).

reactions.description: Override or suppress the kind-driven default reactions.

tools.name: canvas_screenshot
tools.description: Capture an image and metadata from the active Bun.WebView session. Start it with canvas_webview action "start" first.

targetBoardId.description: Not supported: screenshots inspect the shared WebView.

format.description: Screenshot format (default depends on Bun; png recommended)
